ai.title: Repair malformed tool call inputs
ai.summary: Agent runtime repairs malformed tool call inputs via stringified JSON parsing and alias normalization. `normalizeReplacementAliases` maps `old_str`/`new_str` to `old`/`new` for `str_replace` and `propose_str_replace` schemas. `parseStringifiedToolInput` attempts up to three `JSON.parse` cycles before applying narrow field repairs for tools like `code_search` and `glob` using a strict allowlist. Scope covers `common/src/tools/params` and `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant asks to search files, replace text, or run code actions, some AI models accidentally mangle the message so badly it arrives broken: the arguments come jumbled, double-encoded, or with slightly wrong names like "old_str" instead of "old". Today, the assistant quietly fixes those broken messages behind the scenes, re-parsing the garbled text up to three times and mapping the wrong names back to the right ones before deciding what you actually asked for. You'd notice fewer times the assistant refuses a command or fails mid-task complaining it couldn't understand you.

ai.title: Default freebuff to DeepSeek V4 Pro, switch lite to Kimi
ai.summary: Freebuff default model updated to DeepSeek V4 Pro; Lite mode defaults to Kimi. Logic in `agents/base2/base2.ts` and `agents/editor/editor.ts` refactored to handle new variants and conditional Gemini Thinker spawning. CLI components (`freebuff-model-selector.tsx`, `waiting-room-screen.tsx`) updated to reflect new defaults and warning display logic. `local-agent-registry.ts` uses new helper `canFreebuffModelSpawnGeminiThinker` to strip spawnable agents for non-reasoning models.

eli5.text: When you start a free coding assistant session, it will now run on a model called DeepSeek V4 Pro instead of the previous default. If you explicitly ask for the lighter 'lite' mode, that picks a different model called Kimi. The picker screen you use to choose a model will show an extra line of caution next to any model that collects data, so you can spot it before confirming. These defaults are live now for anyone starting a new free or lite session.

ai.title: Kimi k2.6 gated to deployment hours
ai.summary: Kimi k2.6 added to FIREWORKS_HOURS_GATED_MODELS in web/src/llm-api/fireworks.ts. Restricts access to freebuff deployment hours on serverless, matching legacy GLM 5.1 behavior. Ensures consistent availability windows for specific models.

eli5.text: When you use the freebuff deployment during its scheduled hours, a newly added model called Kimi k2.6 is now restricted to those same hours, joining the older GLM 5.1 model that was already limited this way. This means that outside of freebuff deployment hours, you cannot access Kimi k2.6 through the serverless option, and you will get a clear model_unavailable error if you try. The change is live today, and it only affects users attempting to use Kimi k2.6 or GLM 5.1 outside of the designated freebuff deployment hours.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.646 ships DeepSeek V4 Pro default and model
ai.summary: The Codebuff release version was bumped from 1.0.645 to 1.0.646 in `cli/release/package.json`. This release packages several user-visible changes since 1.0.645, including defaulting Freebuff to DeepSeek V4 Pro with Lite mode falling back to Kimi, restoring the Gemini Thinker subagent for Kimi free sessions, and adding the `gravity_index` and `render_ui` tools for third-party integration discovery and interactive CLI buttons. The CLI model selector now displays daily rate limit usage ('Used today' and 'Limit used') instead of dynamic queue depth hints, and focused rows in the waiting room rely on a green border and arrow rather than green text coloring.
ai.evidence: The diff shows only `cli/release/package.json` changed, bumping the version string from 1.0.645 to 1.0.646. The version bump is a release packaging increment, as described in the analysis notes: 'Bump version to 1.0.646'.

eli5.text: This release makes DeepSeek's V4 Pro AI model the default choice for free users, giving you a powerful new reasoning-focused assistant out of the box, while the lighter-weight Kimi model now handles quick, streamlined tasks by default. You gain better control over which models you use, with the model picker now showing how close each AI is to hitting its daily usage limits, so you won't unexpectedly run out of credits mid-conversation. Interactive buttons can now appear directly in your terminal, letting agents offer single-tap links to set up third-party service connections like API keys or sign-ups. Tool naming and input handling got more reliable, meaning fewer glitches when the AI calls specialized helpers, and the new gravity_index search makes discovering and reporting on integrated services faster. Upgrading means smoother, more responsive conversations with clearer feedback about your free-tier limits, plus access to interactive prompts and a sturdier agent engine that recovers gracefully from common input mistakes. Whether you're building code, debugging, or just chatting with AI, you get the latest default model (DeepSeek V4 Pro) without lifting a finger, and the option to swap in Kimi or Gemini when the situation calls for it.

ai.title: Bump Freebuff CLI to 0.0.54 with model defaults and tool fixes
ai.summary: Version 0.0.54 bundles the model and tool improvements shipped since 0.0.53. Default freebuff switches to DeepSeek V4 Pro while lite mode defaults to Kimi, with conditional Gemini Thinker spawning updated across `agents/base2/base2.ts` and `agents/editor/editor.ts`. The agent runtime now repairs malformed tool call inputs via stringified JSON parsing and alias normalization, and subagent tool names use underscores instead of hyphens via the new `getAgentToolName` helper. Kimi K2.6 replaces GLM 5.1 as the free default model, and the CLI model selector now shows rate limits with simplified navigation.
ai.evidence: Commit 163e3485 modifies `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, incrementing the version field from 0.0.53 to 0.0.54. This is a release-bump commit with a single line change (+1/-1).

eli5.text: This release adds new AI models and smarter agent tools to Freebuff. DeepSeek V4 Pro is now the default model for Freebuff, while Kimi K2.6 replaces GLM 5.1 as the free tier model for lighter agents. You can now click interactive buttons in the terminal that open links in your browser, such as a button to get your API key for a service. The built-in agent tool names now use underscores for better compatibility with model providers. The CLI model picker now shows your current usage and quota limits so you can see how close you are to hitting your limit. Additionally, malformed tool calls are repaired automatically, so agents can recover from bad input without failing.

ai.title: Enable reasoning replay in agent runtime message history
ai.summary: The `INCLUDE_REASONING_IN_MESSAGE_HISTORY` flag in `packages/agent-runtime/src/constants.ts` is set to `true`. This causes reasoning chunks emitted by the model to be appended to the assistant message history, allowing them to replay on subsequent turns. Consecutive reasoning chunks are consolidated into a single message. This change affects the agent runtime's context management and model input.

eli5.text: The agent runtime now saves the reasoning thoughts the model generates while answering, and replays them as part of the conversation history on the next turn. If you look at a multi-turn conversation, you will see the model's internal reasoning from earlier turns carried forward to inform its next response. This only affects the agent runtime's behavior today, as the flag controlling it has been flipped on in the constants file.

ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release version is bumped from `0.0.54` to `0.0.55` in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` as a routine release increment. This release ships the notable change where `INCLUDE_REASONING_IN_MESSAGE_HISTORY` is set to `true` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/constants.ts`, causing reasoning chunks emitted by the model to be appended to the assistant message history for replay on subsequent turns. Consecutive reasoning chunks are consolidated into a single message within the agent runtime's context management. The version bump itself contains no other source changes beyond the package version string.
ai.evidence: Commit [ce8a4ade] modifies `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, incrementing the `version` field from `0.0.54` to `0.0.55`. The release includes the notable `INCLUDE_REASONING_IN_MESSAGE_HISTORY` flag being set to `true` in `packages/agent-runtime/src/constants.ts`, which appends reasoning chunks to the assistant message history for replay on subsequent turns. eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.55 now remembers what the AI was thinking about during a task, so conversations with your code assistant flow more naturally across multiple turns. The model's internal reasoning steps, which are usually discarded between messages, are now saved in the conversation history and reused when needed, making multi-step coding discussions less repetitive. This means follow-up questions and corrections work better because context from earlier reasoning is preserved instead of being lost. By upgrading, you get a smarter assistant that keeps track of its own thought process throughout extended coding sessions.

ai.summary: Version `1.0.647` of the Freebuff CLI (`codebuff` package in `cli/release/package.json`) succeeds `1.0.646`. This release bundles the notable change of enabling reasoning replay: the `INCLUDE_REASONING_IN_MESSAGE_HISTORY` flag in `packages/agent-runtime/src/constants.ts` is now `true`, causing model-emitted reasoning chunks to be appended to assistant message history and consolidated into a single message for replay on subsequent turns. Consecutive reasoning chunks are merged so they do not duplicate in context.
ai.evidence: Commit [48f615e8] bumps the version field in `cli/release/package.json` from `1.0.646` to `1.0.647`. The diff is a single-line change to the `version` property of the `codebuff` release manifest.

eli5.text: This release strengthens how the assistant keeps track of its own thinking process across a conversation. The reasoning steps the AI generates while working through a problem are now saved into the conversation history, so they replay on later turns instead of being lost. This means complex, multi-step tasks stay coherent and don't have to restart their internal reasoning from scratch each time you ask a follow-up question. Upgrading gives you a more consistent and reliable assistant that remembers its train of thought, reducing repetitive analysis and producing better answers on long, involved tasks.

ai.title: Remove live queue position hints from CLI model selector
ai.summary: The CLI model selector now hides "N ahead" counts, relying on static status labels like "Closed" and "Limit used" instead. Traffic levels do not currently trigger queue formation, making the dynamic depth hints noisy and visually cluttering. The change updates `cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx` and `common/src/constants/freebuff-models.ts` (Kimi tagline shift). The `queueDepthByModel` field in `common/src/types/freebuff-session.ts` is retained in the API response for diagnostics but is no longer consumed by the UI.

eli5.text: When you open the model picker in the CLI, you've probably seen lines like 'Kimi K2.6, 3 ahead' telling you how many people are supposedly in line. That counter is gone now: rows just show the model name plus a short status like 'Closed' (when it's outside its scheduled hours) or 'Limit used' (when your personal quota is burned through). The data still comes back from the server, but nothing in the interface reads it anymore, so you won't see a number change anywhere, the picker is just cleaner and a bit narrower, with secondary details tucking onto a second line when your terminal is too small for one row. One unrelated tweak landed in the same snapshot: the Kimi K2.6 tagline flipped from 'Smart' to 'Balanced' in the picker's constant list, so that label (if the interface shows it) now

ai.title: Simplify CLI model selector focus styling
ai.summary: Removed conditional green text coloring for focused rows in cli/src/components/freebuff-model-selector.tsx. The focus indicator now relies solely on the green border and arrow, keeping the model name in standard foreground/muted colors. This change applies to the CLI waiting room UI only. No functional logic or state changes were made.

eli5.text: The list of models you can pick from while you wait in the CLI tool no longer turns the model name green when it's selected. Instead, a green border and arrow point to the chosen model, while the name itself stays in its normal color, so the highlight is quieter and the text doesn't jump out at you. This only affects the waiting-room screen you see when using the command-line tool before you get connected.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.56 CLI release drops queue hints and simplifies focus
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI release version was bumped from 0.0.55 to 0.0.56 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`. This release ships two CLI-visible changes: the model selector now hides dynamic "N ahead" counts, relying on static status labels instead, and focused rows in the waiting-room UI no longer use green text coloring, keeping only the green border and arrow as focus indicators. The `queueDepthByModel` field remains in the API response for diagnostics but is no longer consumed by the UI.
ai.evidence: Version field in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json` changed from "0.0.55" to "0.0.56"; release updates include hiding live queue position hints in the CLI model selector and simplified focus styling.

eli5.text: Freebuff 0.0.56 makes the model picker in the CLI cleaner and less cluttered when you're choosing which AI model to use. The selector now hides the old "X models ahead of you" wait-count labels, so the list only shows clear status tags like "Closed" or "Limit used" instead. Focused model rows no longer fade the model name into green text, relying on a green border and arrow to show what is selected, which keeps names readable. The underlying API still reports queue-depth data for diagnostics, but the visual hints that created noise have been turned off. Upgrading gives you a less distracting and simpler model-selection experience in the waiting-room screen, especially when traffic levels don't actually build real queues.
